NITER hosts more than ten active student clubs and societies — including the Computer Club, Science Society, Career Club, Language Club, Cultural Club, Games & Sports Club, Islamic Society, Robotics Club, Film and Photography Club, Journalism Society and Social Welfare Club. Historically, club activity was scattered across Facebook pages, WhatsApp and Messenger groups and word of mouth, which made it difficult for students to discover clubs, apply for membership, follow notices and register for events.

The NITER Clubs Portal gives every club a single, professional, always-available home online. Students can browse all clubs, read live notices, fill membership and event forms, export their own submissions, and file complaints. Club executives and admins get a member portal where they publish notices, build forms, review submissions, manage complaints and administer roles — all in real time, with no developer required.
• Establish a credible, permanent web presence for every club, independent of any single social platform.
• Reduce the manual overhead of membership drives, event registrations and announcements.
• Increase event attendance and membership sign-ups through better visibility and live feedback.
• Let club executives publish an event, notice or sponsored ad in under five minutes without touching code.
• Protect student data — personal information is visible only to club staff, never to the public.

13.1 NITER AI — The AI Copilot (the flagship)

NITER AI is a built-in assistant that runs entirely in the browser and works offline. It combines a deep NITER knowledge base with agentic actions, coding, documents, scheduling and a self-improving memory — so it is as useful for asking "when's the next robotics meetup?" as it is for "convert the C bubble sort to Rust" or "make cover pages for the whole class".
The institute, all 5 departments and their syllabi, the RMG/textile industry, BTMA, campus and bus service, the full faculty directory (~106 staff), fees, hostels, scholarships, news and every club.

RSVP to events, follow clubs, build to-do lists ("remind me to prepare slides"), auto-fill and submit membership forms from the student's identity, and create events from plain English — "Robotics workshop, Thursday 3pm, Lab 2, free pizza" becomes a scheduled event with a poster draft and RSVP form. Ask "how am I doing on my list?" for a live progress bar.
Damerau-Levenshtein typo tolerance with "Did you mean" bubbles; it learns every misspelling → correction

14. v4.0: Math Engine, Document Intelligence & Campus Knowledge

Version 4.0 extends NITER AI with three new capability areas: a full offline math engine, an attach-and-read document pipeline with industry-grade OCR, and expanded official-source campus knowledge with live, time-aware answers. Everything is processed locally in the browser - nothing you upload ever leaves your machine.

NITER AI can now solve mathematics directly in the chat, fully offline, before the code vault or knowledge base runs. Answers render as styled cards with step-by-step rules, a .docx export button and the "How I reasoned" panel; shortcuts live in the LIVE NOW rail.
Equations: linear ("solve 2x+3=7") and quadratic ("x²-5x+6=0") with the discriminant shown.
Calculus: derivatives ("differentiate x^3") and indefinite integrals ("integrate 2x dx") with the power rule and antiderivative steps.
Percentages: of, increase/decrease and "what percent of 200 is 50".
Number theory: factorials, primality, GCD/LCM, prime factors, mean/range/standard deviation.
Geometry and trigonometry: circle area/circumference, Pythagoras, exact sin/cos/tan values.
Unit conversions: km↔miles, kg↔lbs, °C↔°F, hours↔minutes and more, plus expression evaluation at a point and function calls (log, ln, sqrt, cbrt).

NITER AI accepts attachments through the 📎 button or drag-and-drop in both the floating window and the full-page view. Uploaded files become a session document the assistant can understand and answer questions about.

Images → OCR with Tesseract.js (the standard client OCR engine); PDFs → text-layer extraction with pdf.js; .docx → a hand-rolled ZIP + native DecompressionStream parser (no libraries, fully offline); .txt/.md/.csv/.json read directly.
Document understanding: extractive summaries, data mining (emails, phone numbers, names, dates, URLs), word/page/character stats, and a rough Bangla translation of the opening.
File cards in chat show a thumbnail, page/character counts and a collapsible extracted-text viewer; the document persists across reloads and clears with the chat.
Privacy: all processing is in-browser; OCR/PDF engines lazy-load from CDN only on first use and degrade gracefully when offline.

Deep, official-source entries for the everyday facilities students actually ask about, plus a live time-aware status for the library.
